items.text: When a supervised task has not completed an execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own, the supervisor software shall detect an alive fault (fault code 1) for that task.
The supervisor software shall start alive supervision when the start-up integrity checks have passed.

items.rationale: The system time limit of 100 µs for detection is allocated entirely to the supervisor software, because the detection is a software comparison of the measured start delay with the configured start limit (no hardware share is stated in the system requirements).
items.text: When a supervised task has not started when its configured start limit after its release has expired, the supervisor software shall detect a late start fault (fault code 2) for that task no later than 100 µs after the start limit expires, verified by test with margins of at least 200 µs on either side of the start limit.

items.rationale: The system time limit of 100 µs for detection is allocated entirely to the supervisor software, because the detection is a software comparison of the measured execution time with the configured execution limit.
items.text: When a supervised task is still executing after its configured execution limit has expired, the supervisor software shall detect an overrun fault (fault code 3) for that task no later than 100 µs after the execution limit expires, verified by test with margins of at least 200 µs on either side of the execution limit.

The supervisor software shall treat a measured start delay equal to the configured start limit as within the limit, so that a late start fault is detected only when the measured start delay is greater than the limit.

The supervisor software shall treat a measured execution time equal to the configured execution limit as within the limit, so that an overrun fault is detected only when the measured execution time is greater than the limit.
The supervisor software shall measure the start delay of each supervised task with a resolution of 100 µs.
The supervisor software shall measure the execution time of each supervised task with a resolution of 100 µs.

At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle are missing or have not arrived in the configured release order, the supervisor software shall detect a program flow fault (fault code 4).

For a program flow fault (code 4), the supervisor software shall send one fault report per control cycle, with the entity being the task expected at the first position at which the received checkpoint differs from the configured release order or is missing.
The default configuration data shall define exactly four supervised tasks: the 10 ms tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, and the 100 ms task T_DIAG.
The default configuration data shall define the release order of the 10 ms tasks in each 10 ms period as T_IN, then T_CTRL, then T_OUT.
The default configuration data shall define the release of T_DIAG after T_OUT in every tenth 10 ms period.
The default configuration data shall define a start limit of 2 ms after release for each of T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT and T_DIAG.
The default configuration data shall define an execution limit of 3 ms for each of T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT.
The default configuration data shall define an execution limit of 20 ms for T_DIAG.

The supervisor software shall take the set of supervised tasks and their periods, timing limits and release order from configuration data, so that a change of any of them requires no change to the supervisor code.

When, at start-up, a configuration value is outside its allowed range (a timing limit longer than its task period, a zero period or an unknown task), the supervisor software shall detect a configuration fault (fault code 9, entity CONFIG).
When the supervisor software detects a configuration fault (fault code 9) at start-up, it shall latch the safe state.
From the instant a fault is detected, the supervisor software shall not service the independent watchdog or the window watchdog until the next reset.

items.rationale: Per CON-SUP-148 the supervisor configures and starts the independent watchdog only through the start service of the IWDG driver. It relies on that service to write the prescaler selection and the reload value taken from the configuration structure (DRV-IWDG-001, DRV-IWDG-029); the supervisor software supplies the configuration that gives the 100 ms timeout and does not restate the driver's hardware obligations.
items.text: The supervisor software shall use the independent watchdog, running from its own clock, configured with a timeout of 100 ms.
The supervisor software shall use the window watchdog configured so that it causes a reset when a refresh arrives earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh.
While every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected since the last reset, the supervisor software shall refresh the window watchdog once at the end of each control cycle.

items.rationale: Per CON-SUP-148 the supervisor refreshes the independent watchdog only through the refresh service of the IWDG driver, which issues the counter reload request (DRV-IWDG-006).
items.text: While every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected since the last reset, the supervisor software shall service the independent watchdog so that no independent watchdog reset occurs.

items.rationale: Per CON-SUP-148 the services are made through the refresh service of the IWDG driver (DRV-IWDG-006). Closes the independent watchdog part of OP-SYS-002 (deferred to sw-req). The IWDG timeout is 100 ms (SYS-SUP-011), so during a fault-free start-up every interval without a service must stay below it. Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r5-001: the three interval obligations are split so each is judged on its own; this requirement holds the interval between consecutive services, SWR-WDG-013 holds the interval from activation to the first service and SWR-WDG-014 holds the interval from the last service to the end of start-up, with the same 100 ms limit and the same no-fault condition. Together they also force at least one service when start-up lasts 100 ms or longer. The margin and the way the servicing is scheduled while the integrity checks run are left to sw-arch and sw-design (OP-SWR-001).
items.text: During a start-up in which no fault is detected, the supervisor software shall make the interval between any two consecutive services of the independent watchdog shorter than 100 ms.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-006 (F-sw-req-item-r5-001). Per CON-SUP-148 the services are made through the refresh service of the IWDG driver (DRV-IWDG-006). The IWDG timeout is 100 ms (SYS-SUP-011), so the first service must come before it elapses from activation. Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r6-001: the bound is the same 100 ms from activation whether the first service falls during start-up or, when no service is made during start-up, after the end of start-up under SWR-WDG-005; the statement now says so, so a start-up shorter than 100 ms is not read differently. Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r7-001: the obligation is conditioned on no fault having been detected up to the first service; once a fault is detected before it, SWR-WDG-001 and SYS-SUP-010 prohibit servicing until reset, so the 100 ms obligation lapses and the two do not conflict (the watchdog reset then follows). A first service during start-up is therefore permitted, not required. Reworked for F-sw-req-set-r3-001: the statement holds only the first-service timing obligation; the withholding of service after a fault is specified by SWR-WDG-001 alone and is no longer restated here. SWR-WDG-014 applies only when a service was made during start-up. Scheduling is left to sw-arch and sw-design (OP-SWR-001).
items.text: While no fault has been detected since the last reset, the supervisor software shall make the interval from the activation of the independent watchdog to its first service shorter than 100 ms, where the first service may occur either during start-up or after the end of start-up under SWR-WDG-005, and the 100 ms bound applies in both cases.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-006 (F-sw-req-item-r5-001). Per CON-SUP-148 the services are made through the refresh service of the IWDG driver (DRV-IWDG-006). The IWDG timeout is 100 ms (SYS-SUP-011); the interval after the last start-up service ends where normal servicing under SWR-WDG-005 begins. The end of start-up is defined as in SWR-WDG-006 before the split. If no service was made during start-up, the interval from activation is bounded by SWR-WDG-013. Scheduling is left to sw-arch and sw-design (OP-SWR-001).
items.text: During a start-up in which no fault is detected and the independent watchdog has been serviced, the supervisor software shall make the interval from the last service of the independent watchdog to the end of start-up shorter than 100 ms, where the end of start-up is the point at which the start-up integrity checks are complete and the supervisor software begins servicing the independent watchdog under SWR-WDG-005.

items.rationale: Added for F-sw-req-set-r3-002 (SQ-01). CON-SUP-148 allows configuring, starting and refreshing the independent watchdog only through the IWDG driver services. The start service takes the configuration structure (prescaler selection and reload value, DRV-IWDG-001, DRV-IWDG-029; it starts the watchdog, DRV-IWDG-015); the refresh service issues the counter reload request (DRV-IWDG-006, DRV-IWDG-047). The requirement states the exclusive use at software level and does not restate the driver's hardware obligations. SWR-WDG-002 and SWR-WDG-005 give the 100 ms configuration and the servicing obligation that are realised through these services.
items.text: The supervisor software shall use only the services of the IWDG driver for every access to the independent watchdog peripheral.

items.rationale: Closes the window watchdog part of OP-SYS-002 (deferred to sw-req) as far as the inputs decide it. Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r1-002: SYS-SUP-015 forbids any window watchdog reset during fault-free start-up, and the window watchdog resets on a late refresh (12 ms, SYS-SUP-012) as well as an early one (6 ms), so the requirement now obliges a refresh before the window expires, not only a timing limit on refreshes made. It applies whenever the window watchdog is enabled, so it stays correct whether the window watchdog is enabled before or only at the first control cycle; if it is not enabled during start-up, no window watchdog reset can occur and the requirement is vacuously met. Whether it is enabled before the first control cycle, and the mechanism that provides the refreshes while the integrity checks run, are not decided in the inputs and are recorded as OP-SWR-001 (deferred to sw-arch). Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r2-001: the inputs do not state whether the window watchdog hardware applies the early limit to the first refresh after enabling, so the requirement treats the enabling instant as the previous refresh and requires the first refresh no earlier than 6 ms after it; this is safe whether or not the hardware applies the early limit there, and no hardware fact is assumed. The exact hardware behaviour remains open in OP-SWR-001 (deferred to sw-arch). Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r2-002: the transition from the last start-up refresh to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 is split out as SWR-WDG-008. Reworked for F-sw-req-item-r3-001: OP-SWR-001 permits enabling only at the first control cycle, so start-up may end before any refresh. In that case there is no previous refresh, so the enabling instant is the reference as above: the interval from enabling to the end of start-up is bounded by the 12 ms limit, and the transition to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 is bounded from the enabling instant to 6 ms through 12 ms. SWR-WDG-008 covers the transition only when a refresh occurred during start-up. Reworked for F-sw-req-set-r1-001 and F-sw-req-set-r1-002: this requirement now holds only the consecutive-refresh bound; the first refresh after enabling, the last refresh to the end of start-up, and the no-refresh-during-start-up case are split out as SWR-WDG-009, SWR-WDG-010 and SWR-WDG-011 with the same bounds, each conditioned on no fault having been detected (SWR-WDG-001: no servicing from fault detection until reset), consistently with SWR-WDG-008.
items.text: During start-up, while the window watchdog is enabled and for as long as no fault has been detected, the supervisor software shall make every interval between two consecutive refreshes of the window watchdog no shorter than 6 ms and no longer than 12 ms.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-007 for F-sw-req-item-r2-002: SWR-WDG-007 bounds the refresh intervals inside start-up and SWR-WDG-004 starts the normal refreshes, so the interval across the transition needs its own bound, in the window of SYS-SUP-012, to avoid a window watchdog reset (SYS-SUP-015). If a fault is detected before the first refresh, SWR-WDG-001 applies, no refresh is made and this requirement does not apply (no servicing after detection). If the window watchdog was not refreshed during start-up, the first refresh after enabling is bounded by SWR-WDG-007 and this requirement does not apply. The control cycle period is not restated here; it is given by the configuration (SWR-CFG-007) and the architecture must schedule the first refresh accordingly.
items.text: During a start-up in which the window watchdog has been refreshed, and for as long as no fault has been detected up to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004, the supervisor software shall make the interval from the last refresh during start-up to that first refresh no shorter than 6 ms and no longer than 12 ms.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-007 (F-sw-req-set-r1-002). The enabling instant is treated as the previous refresh, as the inputs do not state whether the hardware applies the early limit to the first refresh (OP-SWR-001, deferred to sw-arch). Conditioned on no fault so far, consistently with SWR-WDG-001 (F-sw-req-set-r1-001).
items.text: During start-up, when the window watchdog is enabled and for as long as no fault has been detected up to its first refresh, the supervisor software shall make the interval from enabling the window watchdog to its first refresh no shorter than 6 ms and no longer than 12 ms.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-007 (F-sw-req-set-r1-002). Bounds the interval from the last start-up refresh to the end of start-up so the window does not expire; the end of start-up is the point at which the start-up integrity checks are complete and the supervisor software begins the refreshes under SWR-WDG-004. Conditioned on no fault detected, consistently with SWR-WDG-001 (F-sw-req-set-r1-001). The transition to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 is SWR-WDG-008.
items.text: During a start-up in which the window watchdog has been refreshed, and for as long as no fault has been detected up to the end of start-up, the supervisor software shall make the interval from the last refresh to the end of start-up no longer than 12 ms, where the end of start-up is the point at which the start-up integrity checks are complete and the supervisor software begins the refreshes under SWR-WDG-004.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-007 (F-sw-req-set-r1-002). Covers the case where start-up ends before any refresh (OP-SWR-001 permits enabling only at the first control cycle): the enabling instant is the reference. Conditioned on no fault detected, consistently with SWR-WDG-001 (F-sw-req-set-r1-001). The end of start-up is as defined in SWR-WDG-010. Split for IQ-11 (one shall per requirement): the bound from enabling to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004 is SWR-WDG-012.
items.text: During a start-up in which the window watchdog is enabled but not refreshed, and for as long as no fault has been detected, the supervisor software shall make the interval from enabling the window watchdog to the end of start-up no longer than 12 ms, where the end of start-up is the point at which the start-up integrity checks are complete and the supervisor software begins the refreshes under SWR-WDG-004.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-WDG-011 for IQ-11. Covers the case where start-up ends before any refresh (OP-SWR-001 permits enabling only at the first control cycle): the enabling instant is the reference for the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004, with the 6 ms to 12 ms window of SYS-SUP-012. Conditioned on no fault detected, consistently with SWR-WDG-001.
items.text: During a start-up in which the window watchdog is enabled but not refreshed, and for as long as no fault has been detected up to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004, the supervisor software shall make the interval from enabling the window watchdog to that first refresh no shorter than 6 ms and no longer than 12 ms.

At start-up before any task is released, the supervisor software shall compute the CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) over the program code from linker symbol __app_start up to and excluding the byte at linker symbol __app_end, taken in increasing address order, and compare it with the 32 bit little-endian reference word stored at linker symbol __app_crc, outside that range.

When the start-up program code check finds that the computed CRC-32 differs from the stored reference, the supervisor software shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up (fault code 5, entity CODE).

At start-up before any task is released, the supervisor software shall compute the CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) over the configuration data block from linker symbol __cfg_start up to and excluding the byte at linker symbol __cfg_end, taken in increasing address order, and compare it with the 32 bit little-endian reference word stored at linker symbol __cfg_crc, outside that range.
When the start-up configuration check finds that the computed CRC-32 differs from the stored one, the supervisor software shall detect a configuration integrity fault (fault code 6, entity CONFIG).
The supervisor software shall not release any supervised task until both start-up integrity checks have passed.

While the application runs, the supervisor software shall process the range __app_start to __app_end one segment per control cycle in increasing address order, the first segment of a pass starting at __app_start, each later segment starting at the byte after the end of the previous segment, the first segment of the next pass following the last segment of the previous pass, and each segment being 1 KiB long except the last segment of an image whose length is not a multiple of 1 KiB, which contains only the remaining bytes and no byte outside the range.

While the application runs, the supervisor software shall, at the end of each run-time pass over all segments, have determined the CRC-32/MPEG-2 value, with initial value 0xFFFFFFFF and bytes taken in increasing address order, of the whole range __app_start up to and excluding the byte at __app_end, as one value over the whole range and not as separate values per segment.
The run-time program code check shall use at most 0.5 ms of processor time in each control cycle.

When a completed run-time pass over the program code yields a CRC-32 that differs from the stored reference, the supervisor software shall detect a run-time code integrity fault (fault code 7, entity CODE).
The application image from linker symbol __app_start up to and excluding the byte at linker symbol __app_end shall be at most 1 MiB long.
While the application runs, the supervisor software shall complete a full run-time check pass over a program code image of 1 MiB within 11 s.

items.rationale: Software share of the 50 ms reaction time of SYS-SUP-024: 49 ms, as stated in SYS-SUP-025 (the remaining 1 ms is the board output stage, SYS-SUP-086).
items.text: When a fault of fault code 1, fault code 2, fault code 3, fault code 4, fault code 5, fault code 6, fault code 7 or fault code 9 is detected, the supervisor software shall change the control output pins and the status signal pin to the low level within 49 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable.

items.rationale: Split per CON-SUP-132: from reset until software configures the pins they are inputs and the low level is provided by external board pull-down resistors (hardware dependency, not a software obligation). The software obligation starts when it configures the pins, which it does before any other start-up step (configuration of the pins is required by SWR-SAF-003; split from this item for IQ-11, one shall per requirement).
items.text: After any reset, the supervisor software shall keep both control outputs and the status signal driven low from the instant it configures them as outputs (SWR-SAF-003) until the start-up integrity checks have passed. The low level before that configuration depends on the external pull-down resistors and is not provided by the software.
After a reset, the supervisor software shall configure the two control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low before any other start-up step.

When the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault has been detected since the last reset and the safe-state latch is not set, the supervisor software shall drive the status signal high (operational).
While the safe-state latch is set, including after a software reset or a watchdog reset, the supervisor software shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low.

While the safe-state latch is set, including after a software reset or a watchdog reset and after the start-up integrity checks have passed, the supervisor software shall not release any supervised task.
From any reset until it configures them as outputs (SWR-SAF-003), the supervisor software shall leave the microcontroller pins of the two control outputs and the status signal as inputs.

When a fault with fault code 1, fault code 2, fault code 3, fault code 4, fault code 5, fault code 6 or fault code 7 is detected as the first or second detection of that fault code counted since its detection count was last zero (SWR-LAT-008), and both the fault report and the entry into the safe state complete before any watchdog reset occurs, the supervisor software shall request a software reset within 20 ms after the later of the completion of the fault report and the entry into the safe state; if a watchdog reset occurs before both have completed, no software reset request is required.

When a fault with fault code 1, fault code 2, fault code 3, fault code 4, fault code 5, fault code 6 or fault code 7 is detected as the third detection of that fault code counted since its detection count was last zero (SWR-LAT-008), the supervisor software shall set the safe-state latch, which holds until the next power-on reset.

When a fault with fault code 1, fault code 2, fault code 3, fault code 4, fault code 5, fault code 6 or fault code 7 is detected as the third detection of that fault code counted since its detection count was last zero (SWR-LAT-008), the supervisor software shall not request a software reset.

When a fault code 8 report is made at start-up and it is the third detection of fault code 8 counted since the detection count of fault code 8 was last zero (SWR-LAT-008), the supervisor software shall set the safe-state latch, which holds until the next power-on reset.
The supervisor software shall keep a separate detection count for each fault code, so that a detection of a different code neither resets nor advances it.

The supervisor software shall count fault-free operating time only while in the OPERATIONAL state, with an under-count of at most 10 ms per reset and at most 100 µs per update, and never with an over-count.
The supervisor software shall retain the safe-state latch across software resets and watchdog resets.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-LAT-007 for F-sw-req-item-r1-005: retention of the detection counts is verifiable separately from the latch and the fault history.
items.text: The supervisor software shall retain the per-code detection counts across software resets and watchdog resets.

items.rationale: Split from SWR-LAT-007 for F-sw-req-item-r1-005: retention of the fault history is verifiable separately from the latch and the detection counts.
items.text: The supervisor software shall retain the fault history across software resets and watchdog resets.

Except at a power-on reset (SWR-LAT-009), the supervisor software shall return a fault code's detection count to zero only after 60 s of fault-free operation, being time in the OPERATIONAL state since the most recent detection of any fault code, and no later than the end of that 60 s extended by the time lost to under-counting (at most 10 ms per reset and at most 100 µs per update of the fault-free operating time).
At a power-on reset, the supervisor software shall clear the safe-state latch, the per-code detection counts and the fault history.

When a fault code 8 report is made at start-up, the supervisor software shall not enter the safe state because of the report itself; the only effect of a code 8 report on the outputs is the safe-state latch set under SWR-LAT-004 at the third detection of code 8, which SWR-SAF-005 then holds.
When a fault code 8 report is made at start-up, the supervisor software shall continue the start-up.
When a fault code 8 report is made at start-up, the supervisor software shall count it as a detection of code 8 toward the latch rule.
After any reset, the supervisor software shall classify the reset cause at start-up from the reset flags as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor (software) reset or other.

After a reset, the supervisor software shall transmit the start-up message RST,<cause> terminated by a line feed on the diagnostic serial line, with <cause> one of POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW or OTHER naming the class of the reset, within 10 ms of the instant start-up classified the reset cause.

When, at start-up, the reset cause is classified as an independent watchdog reset or a window watchdog reset, the supervisor software shall report fault code 8 with the entity IWDG or WWDG respectively as a fault report line FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed on the diagnostic serial line within 10 ms of the instant start-up classified the reset cause, including for a watchdog reset that interrupted the handling of an earlier fault.
When, at start-up, a code 8 report is made, the supervisor software shall transmit the start-up message RST,<cause> on the diagnostic serial line before the code 8 report line.

When a fault is detected, the supervisor software shall transmit on the diagnostic serial line the fault report FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed within 10 ms of the detection, except for a fault interrupted by a watchdog reset before its report and safe-state entry have completed, for which no report is required and only the code 8 report at the next start-up applies.
When an alive fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 1 in the fault report and the name of the task as the entity.
When a late start fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 2 in the fault report and the name of the task as the entity.
When an overrun fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 3 in the fault report and the name of the task as the entity.
When a flow fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 4 in the fault report.
When a code integrity fault at start-up is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 5 in the fault report and the entity CODE.
When a configuration integrity fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 6 in the fault report and the entity CONFIG.
When a code integrity fault at run time is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 7 in the fault report and the entity CODE.
When a watchdog reset fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 8 in the fault report; the entity of that report is given by SWR-RST-003.
When a configuration out of range fault is reported, the supervisor software shall use fault code 9 in the fault report and the entity CONFIG.

The supervisor software shall give <ms since start> in a fault report as an unsigned 32 bit decimal number of milliseconds since the latest reset of any kind, wrapping to 0 ms after 4294967295 ms, taken at the instant of detection of the fault, and for fault code 8 at the instant start-up classified the reset cause.

When a fault report is due for transmission after a service request has been received and before the first character of its answer has been transmitted, the supervisor software shall transmit the fault report line on the diagnostic serial line before the first character of that answer.

When a fault report is due for transmission while a line of an answer is being transmitted, the supervisor software shall transmit the fault report line on the diagnostic serial line after the line feed of the answer line in transmission and before any further line of that answer, without interrupting the line in transmission.
The supervisor software shall limit each line of an answer to a service request to at most 40 characters including the terminating line feed.
The supervisor software shall use the diagnostic serial line at 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

When the service request GET RESET is received while no answer is being transmitted, the supervisor software shall answer RST,<cause> with <cause> one of POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW or OTHER, naming the class of the latest reset, within 50 ms measured from receipt of the terminating line feed, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between the request and its answer.

When the service request GET STATUS is received while no answer is being transmitted, the supervisor software shall answer STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms, measured from the instant the terminating line feed is received to the end of the last character of the answer, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between the request and its answer.

From any reset until the start-up checks pass, while no fault has been detected since that reset and the safe-state latch is not set, the supervisor software shall report <state> as STARTUP (a detected fault is reported as SAFE per SWR-SVC-005 and a set latch as LATCHED per SWR-SVC-006, which takes priority); a code 8 report at start-up does not by itself cause SAFE and leaves the reported state at STARTUP.
While the supervisor software is supervising with the start-up checks passed, no fault detected since the last reset and the safe-state latch not set, it shall report <state> as OPERATIONAL.
From the instant a fault is detected until the next reset, while the safe-state latch is not set, the supervisor software shall report <state> as SAFE.
While the safe-state latch is set, the supervisor software shall report <state> as LATCHED, regardless of which other state condition holds.
The supervisor software shall report <fault count> as the number of fault reports since the last power-on reset, retained across software resets and watchdog resets.

When the service request GET FAULTS is received while no answer is being transmitted, the supervisor software shall answer within 50 ms, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between the request and its answer.

When the service request GET FAULTS is received while no answer is being transmitted, the supervisor software shall answer with the most recent eight fault reports made before the instant of that reception and since the last power-on reset (all of them when fewer than eight have been made), oldest first, one per line, followed by a line END, and only the line END when none has been made; a fault report made after that instant is not a line of that answer.
When a fault report is made while eight fault reports are already held, the supervisor software shall replace the oldest fault report held with the new one.

When a service request line other than GET STATUS, GET FAULTS or GET RESET is received, or a request line longer than 32 ASCII characters is received, while no answer is being transmitted, the supervisor software shall answer ERR.
When a service request is received while an answer is still being transmitted, the supervisor software shall not answer that request.
The supervisor software shall count a service request as received when its terminating line feed is received.

The supervisor software shall complete the answer to each service request that it accepts, meaning a request received while no answer is being transmitted, within 50 ms, measured from the instant the terminating line feed is received to the end of the last character of the answer, extended by the transmission time of the fault reports sent between the request and its answer.

In normal operation (no fault and no service request), the supervisor software shall use at most 10 % of the processor time over any 1 s window, measured on the simulator at the configured core clock.

In test builds, the supervisor software shall provide a test hook that injects each of the fault classes of fault code 1, fault code 2, fault code 3, fault code 4, fault code 5, fault code 6, fault code 7, fault code 8 and fault code 9.

items.rationale: Requirements verified by inspection or by analysis are verified by those methods and are not claimed to run on the simulator or host unit tests. Reworked for F-sw-req-set-r1-003: SYS-SUP-054 covers every system requirement verified by test or demonstration. The software provides this support for each system requirement allocated to software, which every software requirement here refines and traces to; software requirements are the software-level means by which those system requirements are verified. System requirements not allocated to software (hardware-only) are outside the software's scope and are verified at system level, not by this requirement.
items.text: The supervisor software shall run on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board, so that every software requirement, and every system requirement allocated to software, whose verification method is test or demonstration can be verified there or on host unit tests.
The production build of the supervisor software shall not contain the fault-injection test hooks.
The supervisor software shall target the STMicroelectronics STM32N657X0 (Arm Cortex-M55) as its microcontroller.
The supervisor software shall be written in C11.
The supervisor software shall not use dynamic memory allocation.
The supervisor software shall not use recursion.

open_points.text: Follows OP-SYS-002 (deferred to sw-req). The inputs do not say whether the window watchdog is already enabled before the first control cycle, nor how the watchdog servicing is scheduled while the start-up integrity checks run over an image of up to 1 MiB. SWR-WDG-006 and SWR-WDG-007 state the observable outcome (every IWDG service-free interval during start-up below 100 ms, from activation to the end of start-up, every WWDG refresh interval 6 ms to 12 ms, and 6 ms to 12 ms from enabling to the first refresh, no more than 12 ms from the last refresh to the end of start-up, and SWR-WDG-008 bounds the transition to the first refresh under SWR-WDG-004; whether the hardware applies the early limit to the first refresh after enabling is also open here, SWR-WDG-007 being conservative about it) and stay correct and verifiable either way; the choice of mechanism (servicing inside the check loop, a timer-driven service, enabling the window watchdog only at the first control cycle) and the margin below 100 ms belong to the architecture and design.
